text:
alex: heads-up — the dashboard p50/p95 for /v1/generate looks wrong; p50 is showing higher than p95 for the eu-west endpoint. anyone seen this before?

maria: hmm that's usually a sign of bad merge logic or sampling mix. can you paste the endpoint + time range query? :eyes:

alex: timeframe = last 30m, route = /v1/generate, env=prod. quick API call returned: p50=320ms, p95=210ms, sample_count=4. UI shows p50=320 and p95=210 too — but that ordering is obviously inverted. link: https://dash/internal/rollups?route=%2Fv1%2Fgenerate&tz=UTC

cheng: if sample_count is tiny we sometimes surface raw bucketized median from a different aggregation window while p95 uses a merged t-digest. mixing raw buckets + tdigest can invert percentiles. did the rollup window change recently?

taylor: I can repro with a smoke query. when requests are low and there are partially-empty shards, our merge code uses a "fast path" that keeps a centroid with zero weight in one branch. that'll nudge the median upward.

alex: can you paste the fast-path snippet? I want to understand how zero-weight centroids survive.

cheng: snippet (from aggregator.cpp):
```
// fast merge when counts below threshold
if (left.count == 0) return right;
if (right.count == 0) return left;
// later we normalize centroids but there was an off-by-one that left a centroid weight = 0
```
that off-by-one came from an optimization to skip normalization when counts==1 — it didn't account for integer truncation.

maria: ok so root cause = centroid weight becoming zero then later gets treated in percentile interpolation, producing non-monotonic CDF. recommended fixes: 1) guard against zero-weight centroids, 2) fall back to recomputing percentiles from raw histogram when sample_count < 50, 3) add a UX hint in the dashboard explaining sampling/approximation.

taylor: +1. I'll open a small PR for the guard and add a metric that counts zero-weight merges. patch: `if (centroid.weight <= 0) drop_centroid();` and increment `rollup.zero_weight_centroids`

alex: for the UX change, can we show a tiny tooltip on the percentile values: "approximate when sample_count < 50 — aggregated percentiles may be imprecise" keeps PMs off our backs.

maria: yep, also add link to docs: /docs/telemetry/percentile-approximation. and add a dashboard annotation for the last 24h so SREs know when we had low-sample windows.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: eng-platform/rollup-fix v2 -> canary on prod (eu-west) at 2632101500.

cheng: action items: taylor = PR for guard + metric; maria = tooltip + docs link; alex = add dashboard annotation for affected window; I'll follow up on a small test harness to fuzz low-count merges.

alex: thanks — will watch canary and report back. :thumbsup:
